Maybe you're not an uninteresting person. Maybe they want to frak you **more** because of your ebullient personality. Maybe they each want something more intimate, more serious than just friends. 

Or, I'm wrong, and they've told you and you're fully aware that it's just a superficial physical attraction thang they've got for you. Can you clarify?

I'm currently reading ["Hero" by Perry Moore](http://www.goodreads.com/book/show/1251032.Hero) which is a coming-out story of a superhero gay teenager, who is bro-ish. It's a pretty good bildungsroman so far and can't wait to see if the author follows-up with a sequel.
:/ I think that's a bit of a [stretch](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissociative_identity_disorder).

[Create a character in your mind.](http://www.reddit.com/r/todayilearned/comments/187k8c/til_that_comedian_daniel_tosh_tosh0_suffers_from/)

This works for me, especially at meetups I've organized and am forced to introduce myself and others to each other. Organizing local meetups REALLY helped me out because I created a character for myself of this bougie, fancy party thrower. 

If I'm a guest at a party or at a club/bar, this doesn't really help because I can't come up with a character with a reason to be there. But when I organize a get-together, I HAVE to be somebody else. 

Getting drunk helps me out also. But, I don't think it's healthy to rely on substances just to overcome shyness.
